title.narrative: Second Community Action for Landscape Management Program for Results

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective (PDO) is to expand area under sustainable land management practices, secure land tenure and increase market linkages in Highland Areas.

This hybrid operation—combining Program-for-Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF)—supports the National Strategic Investment Framework for Sustainable Landscape Management (ESIF 2, 2024–2038) by advancing long-term landscape restoration. It aims to: (i) expand sustainable land management in degraded Highland Areas; (ii) sustain and expand certification, registration, and digitalization of rural land rights in Ethiopia's highlands, including communal forests and grazing lands; and (iii) raise farm incomes and create jobs by strengthening agribusiness value-chain linkages. Primary beneficiaries are smallholder farmers in program watersheds. The program will increase smallholders livelihood security and broaden income earning opportunities. Efforts will be made for the equitable inclusion of all beneficiaries in Community Watershed Users Cooperative Societies (CWUCS) including vulnerable groups such as landless, youth, elderly, and female-headed households.The PforR component will finance watershed-level sustainable land and natural resource management, strengthen rural land administration, improve tenure security for private and communal lands (including selected forests and grazing areas), and catalyze private-sector participation to ensure sustainability. Under Result Area 1 (Participatory Watershed and Forest Management), Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) incentivize scaling up restoration and market linkages by: (1) registering Community Watershed Users Cooperative Societies (CWUCS) with participatory, approved Watershed Management Plans; (2) expanding the area under sustainable landscape management; (3) establishing Participatory Forest Management with legally recognized cooperatives and approved Forest Management Plans; (4) treating acid soils; (5) integrating cooperatives into existing and new value chains within program catchments; and (6) verifying non forest emission reductions. Under Result Area 2 (Rural Land Administration), DLIs focus on expanding and digitizing secure tenure by: (1) issuing Second Level Land Holding Certificates (SLLCs) for individual parcels; (2) issuing SLLCs for communal forests and grazing lands; (3) operationalizing the National Rural Land Administration Information System in program woredas with digitized SLLCs; and (4) increasing connectivity of land administration offices and systems to national digital infrastructure. The IPF component—financed by IDA, SCALE, Nordic Development Fund (NDF), and ENABLE—will provide cross-cutting technical assistance and capacity building across both result areas and the broader government program (ESIF 2). It will support: (i) agribusiness development by linking landholders to agribusinesses; (ii) design and implementation of payment for ecosystem services (PES) schemes; (iii) access to carbon markets; and (iv) Operationalize pilots to promote voluntary land consolidation in Ethiopia's highlands. These pilots involve baseline surveys, voluntary land exchange, and design, testing, and documentation of a computerized platform in real-world conditions. The likelihood and magnitude of risk for the voluntary exchange program pilot have been assessed. The voluntary land exchange will take place in 12 designated kebeles, involving small parcels of land and following a national legal proclamation.Targeted TA will also promote inclusive alternative livelihoods for women and youth through group-based training and livelihood grants; strengthen community capacity to scale ecosystem conservation and carbon sequestration via participatory forest and watershed management; advance land tenure and property rights awareness; and establish community-based performance monitoring. In addition, the operation will enhance MoA and Ethiopia Forest Development (EFD) operational capacity for CALM 2, including: (i) environmental and social risk management; (ii) procurement and financial management; and (iii) monitoring, reporting, and verification, including advanced remote sensing. IFC will complement implementation with integrated upstream and downstream support for agribusiness linkages, value-chain development, and access to finance, strengthening market access and supply chains through its portfolio, pipeline, and early-stage leads. IFC's approach will promote business models that directly engage smallholder farmers and local communities, with close IFC– World Bank collaboration to ensure coordinated delivery.
